description.narrative:
Mission and vision of the UN Global Disability Fund (formerly UNPRPD)
The mission of the Fund is to support countries to accelerate the implementation of the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD) CRPD and disability inclusive SDGs for all persons with disabilities with the full involvement of Organizations of People with Disability (ODPs).
Its vision is that the rights of all persons with disabilities are fully respected, protected and fulfilled, and that all persons with disabilities fully and equitably participate in society.
Strategic Operational Framework (SOF) 2020-2025
The SOF focuses on the Fund as a catalyst, facilitating a multi-stakeholder approach to accelerate the implementation of the CRPD and disability inclusive SDGs with meaningful participation of organizations of persons with disabilities (OPDs).
This will be achieved by encouraging and supporting countries to develop and reform policies, plans, budgets, programs and services to comply with the CRPD and inclusive SDGs by applying both disability-specific and disability-mainstreamed interventions. In addition, the Fund provides an avenue for facilitating and contributing to a unified response at the country level by the UN - advancing the UNs collective response.
The SOF focuses on three intersecting strategic approaches designed to equip national stakeholders with the knowledge and practical tools for disability inclusive policies and services at national level in both development and humanitarian contexts, addresses the gaps in achieving the essential building blocks or preconditions to CRPD implementation, and supports disability mainstreaming of national development plans, seizing political willingness and commitments including SDG implementation. These strategic approaches include:
1.Catalytic funding for national and multi-country joint programing on disability inclusion, which can be further broken down into three workstreams:
-Country-level joint programs to accelerate CRPD implementation: nationally-owned joint programs on national priorities to advance the essential building blocks for CRPD implementation. This includes especially dedicated efforts to ensure a UN coordinated approach/work to disability inclusion in Ukraine (with earmarked funds for this purpose).
-Disability inclusive national development planning and monitoring: dedicated resources to support SDG processes to increase disability inclusion through the UNs collective response.
-Multi-country joint programs to pilot CRPD implementation tools: multi-country joint programs to pilot and test knowledge management tools that provide concrete guidance on workable solutions for CRPD implementation.
2.Knowledge management and lessons learned, through members and others partners, generating and sharing knowledge management tools and systems to address gaps in technical knowledge on the essential building blocks and preconditions for CRPD implementation and program delivery.
3.Context-relevant capacity building to support inclusive systems and policies: the Fund Secretariat identifies capacity building gaps through its implemented joint programs and delivers targeted capacity building through its members, including IDA and IDDC as per their expertise along with other relevant actors to UN country teams (UNCTs), governments and OPDs to secure a unified understanding of the CRPD and how to translate it into practical implementation both in development and humanitarian contexts. Several cross-cutting approaches will be applied across the Fund's operations and strategic approaches, including a targeted push for increased inclusion of underrepresented groups of persons with disabilities, gender equality and fully integrated participation of OPDs.

The United Nations Global Disability Fund (GDF) is a partnership of 11 UN agencies. The UNGDF works to achieve two outcomes: (1) support and build partnerships and capacity development at the country level to promote the implementation of the CRPD; and (2) improve the integration of disability perspectives into the core work of the UN organizations that are part of the UNGDF. The majority of funding from the UNGDF MDTF goes to the country-level program, where UN organizations engage in collaboration with multiple stakeholders to create the conditions for systemic change. The UNGDF works to strengthen the integration of disability perspectives in the UN system and has a mandate to support the implementation of the UN Disability Mainstreaming Strategy (UN-DIS) adopted by the UN Secretary-General in 2019. The current level of support is approximately SEK 30 million per year.

UN Partnership for the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNPRPD) är ett partnerskap bestående av 11 FN-organ. UNPRPD verkar för att uppnå två resultat: (1) stödja och skapa samarbeten och kapacitetsutveckling på nationell nivå för att främja implementeringen av CRPD; och (2) att förbättra integreringen av funktionshinderperspektiv i kärnverksamheten av de FN-organisationer som ingår i UNPRPD. Huvuddelen av medlen från UNPRPD MDTF går till program på nationell nivå där FN-organisationer deltar i samarbete med flera intressenter för att skapa förutsättningar för systemförändring. UNPRPD arbetar för att stärka integrering av funktionshinderperspektiv i FN-systemet och har ett mandat att stödja genomförandet av FN:s strategi för integrering av funktionshinderperspektivet (UN-DIS) som antogs av FN:s generalsekreterare 2019. Nuvarande stödnivå är ca 30 MSEK per år.

The by Sida assessed and approved 2024 Annual Report of the UN Global Disability Fund (UN GDF) - formerly UNPRPD - is an important reminder of the Funds catalytic role in advancing the rights of persons with disabilities globally.
As the only inter-agency pooled funding mechanism dedicated to supporting the implementation of the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD), the UN GDF continues to demonstrate leadership, ambition, and impact in fostering inclusive, equitable, and resilient societies.
Sida takes particular note of the following key achievements:
2024 marked a transformative year for the Fund both operationally and strategically (Sida was cloesly enaged in this process which entailed a reorganization of the Fund). With over $18 million in new funding secured, the UN GDF expanded its reach and influence, welcoming three new UN members and launching its largest ever multi-country initiative in the Pacific.
In total, 57 programs were operational, including 50 national and 7 multi-country joint initiatives, reflecting the Funds broad geographic and thematic scope.
The Fund maintained a strong focus on systems level change, contributing to 23 structural reforms and the development or adoption of 16 laws, policies, strategies, and regulations efforts that directly support the realization of the CRPD. Through its inclusive and multistakeholder programing model, the UN GDF collaborated with 502 Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs) and 94 government ministries, and provided targeted capacity building to over 5,000 stakeholders, including OPD representatives, government officials, and UN staff.
The Fund continued to mainstream gender equality and the inclusion of marginalized and underrepresented groups, with more than 63% of programs featuring dedicated gender outputs. It also made significant strides in humanitarian contexts, including in Ukraine and the State of Palestine, where it responded to urgent needs with tailored, inclusive programing.
The Fund's commitment to knowledge generation and institutional learning was exemplified by the production of 68 knowledge products, including research studies, tools, and technical guidance. The launch of its multi-country program on unpaid care and gender transformative support systems is a noteworthy step in integrating care economics and disability rights.
2024 also marked the official rebranding of the Fund as the UN GDF, reflecting its broader and more dynamic mandate. It introduced new governance structures aimed at enhancing transparency and accountability, and was selected to host the Resilient and Inclusive Cities Hub (RICH) a major milestone in embedding disability inclusion in urban resilience and climate planning.
